source_anchor: Heidegger Sein und Zeit §§15-18 (Zeug, Zuhandenheit) + §§51-53 (Sein-zum-Tode, 1927); SEP "Martin Heidegger" §2.2
instance: Heidegger's analysis of Dasein contrasts the ready-to-hand (zuhanden) mode of dealing with equipment from the present-at-hand (vorhanden) mode of theoretical inspection, and culminates in being-toward-death as the structure that individuates Dasein. State the structural difference between the two modes and explain why being-toward-death cannot be replaced by averaged talk about mortality.

answer_features.claim: ready-to-hand: equipment is transparent and absorbed in a pragmatic context until it breaks
alt_phrasings: tool is invisible until it fails

answer_features.claim: present-at-hand: object becomes a mere thing with properties when the pragmatic flow breaks
being-toward-death individuates because death is non-relational, ownmost, and cannot be delegated
alt_phrasings: das Man cannot die for me

candidate_responses.text: Ready-to-hand: the hammer is transparent in skilled hammering, absorbed into an in-order-to context, only visible when it breaks. Present-at-hand: once it breaks, the hammer becomes a thing with properties (weight, length) for theoretical inspection. Being-toward-death cannot collapse into averaged "people die" talk because death is non-relational and ownmost — no one can die my death for me, which is exactly what individuates Dasein.
Heidegger thinks we should be authentic and confront death.
In skilled use, equipment is transparent. When the flow breaks, it shows up as object-with-properties. Death individuates because it is ownmost and cannot be delegated.
